title: Market Pulse
body_html:
This post reflects my current views on the market, sectors, and internal breadth/momentum. Expect candid, data-driven analysis, peppered with personal insights drawn from years of trading experience. I aim to provide value in every edition, helping you to see the market through a clearer, more informed lens.

What You Can Expect

  • In-Depth Market Analysis: A thorough examination of market trends, key indices, and pivotal turning points.

  • Sector Spotlights: A closer look at the hottest (and not-so-hot) sectors, highlighting opportunities and risks.

  • Breadth and Momentum Insights: Understanding the underlying strength of the market through breadth indicators and momentum metrics.

  • Themes and Setups: A look at the top stocks in terms of relative strength, momentum, trend, volatility, and liquidity to spot themes, setups, and opportunities

Exclusive Features

  • Interactive Spreadsheet: Alongside each post, I’ll link a detailed spreadsheet that tracks breadth and momentum metrics. This will allow you to follow along with the data and see the trends I’m analyzing day-by-day.

  • Quick Video Commentary: To complement the metrics, I’ll also be posting a quick video commentary several days a week. This will provide a more dynamic overview of the market, offering you additional context and clarity.

Market Metrics

Market Backdrop: Positive

The major indices continue to act constructively. Large-cap indices have pushed to new near-term highs while holding above their rising 10-day, 20-day, and 50-day moving averages. The trend remains supportive, with higher highs, higher lows, and no meaningful deterioration in price structure. Mid- and small-cap indices are also continuing to push higher after bouncing from their 50-day moving averages. Overall, there is little concerning price or trend action at the index level.

Technology remains the clear sector and industry group leader, handily outperforming the other sectors from a relative strength perspective. Leadership is also beginning to take shape in other areas, with Real Estate, Financials, Industrials, Healthcare, Materials, and Cyclicals attempting to push higher out of basing patterns. However, many of these groups still lag significantly in terms of momentum and relative strength, so participation is improving but not yet fully convincing.

At the same time, Energy and defensive areas are beginning to weaken. These groups are rolling over and breaking below key moving averages, suggesting money is rotating away from prior leadership or more defensive positioning. That rotation is not necessarily bearish by itself, but it does reinforce the need to focus on the strongest areas rather than forcing trades across the entire market.

Breadth continues to act constructively. Stocks making new near-term highs now outnumber those making new near-term lows, reflecting broader participation in the push higher. That is a healthy development and supports the current advance.

The one missing ingredient is stronger momentum. While momentum readings are positive, they remain well below prior peak levels. In other words, more stocks are participating, but many are grinding higher rather than expanding powerfully. That keeps the market constructive, but not aggressively bullish. The ideal next step would be continued expansion in new highs, further contraction in new lows, and stronger upside momentum across a broader set of groups.

Tactical Plan of Action

1) Trend & Market Structure

The major indices continue to act constructively. Large caps have pushed to new near-term highs while holding above rising 10-day, 20-day, and 50-day moving averages. The trend remains defined by higher highs, higher lows, and supportive moving average structure. Mid- and small-cap indices are also improving after bouncing from their 50-day moving averages and continuing higher.

At the index level, there is no major price or trend concern right now. The market has moved out of correction-repair mode and back into a constructive advance.

Tactical guidance

  • Shift from cautiously constructive to constructive with selectivity.

  • Increase exposure from the prior 50–65% range toward 65–80% of normal, assuming setups are clean and breadth remains supportive.

  • Stay focused on stocks above rising 10-day and 20-day moving averages.

  • Continue using pullbacks, tight consolidations, and clean base breakouts as the preferred entry points.

  • Do not chase late-stage moves that are already extended from the 10-day moving average.

  • If large caps remain above the 10/20-day and mid/small caps continue holding reclaimed moving averages, maintain an offensive posture.

  • If indices begin reversing back below the 10-day and are forming new lows, reduce exposure quickly.

2) Breadth & Momentum: The Throttle

Breadth has improved meaningfully. New near-term highs are now more than double new near-term lows, which shows broader participation. This supports the current advance and suggests the bounce has developed into a healthier continuation move.

The one missing ingredient is stronger upside momentum. Momentum is positive, but still well below prior peak levels. That means the tape is improving, but not yet showing full power across the board.

Tactical guidance

  • Use breadth as permission to press, but let momentum determine how aggressively.

  • If new highs continue expanding and new lows remain contained, exposure can move toward 75–85%.

  • If breadth remains positive but momentum stays tepid, keep exposure closer to 65–75%.

  • If new lows begin expanding again or new highs contract sharply, reduce exposure back toward 50–65%.

  • The market is healthy enough to participate, but not strong enough to abandon discipline.

3) Sector Focus & Rotation

Technology remains the clear leader and should remain the primary focus. It continues to dominate in price, trend, momentum, and relative strength.

Leadership is beginning to broaden into Real Estate, Financials, Industrials, Healthcare, Materials, and Cyclicals, but many of those groups are still working through basing patterns and remain below prior highs. That means they are improving, but not yet equal leaders.

Energy and defensive areas are weakening, rolling over, and breaking below key moving averages. That rotation suggests risk appetite is improving in some areas, but capital is not being rewarded equally across sectors.

Tactical guidance

  • Keep Technology as the top hunting ground.

  • Begin selectively adding exposure to secondary groups only as they break out of bases or reclaim prior highs with improving relative strength.

  • Real Estate, Financials, Industrials, Healthcare, Materials, and Cyclicals should stay on the watchlist, but entries need to be structure-based.

  • Avoid Energy and defensive names that are breaking down through key moving averages.

  • Do not force diversification into weak groups. In this tape, strength should be bought and weakness should be avoided.

4) Stock Selection & Entries

The market is constructive, but because momentum is not yet fully broad, stock selection remains important. The best opportunities are still likely to come from leaders showing strong relative strength, clean structure, and controlled pullbacks.

Prioritize

  • Technology leaders breaking out or setting up from tight bases.

  • Stocks holding above rising 10-day and 20-day moving averages.

  • Names showing relative strength while the broader market grinds higher.

  • Clean 2–5 day tight patterns after a strong move.

  • Pullbacks into support with volume drying up.

  • Secondary-sector leaders emerging from Real Estate, Financials, Industrials, Healthcare, Materials, and Cyclicals.

  • Breakouts from bases with strong volume and improving group strength.

Avoid

  • Energy and defensive names breaking below key moving averages.

  • Stocks making sloppy, low-volume bounces from weak trends.

  • Late entries far above the 10-day moving average.

  • Loose, wide, volatile patterns.

  • Laggards that are still below declining 10-day or 20-day moving averages.

  • Buying secondary groups before they actually break out of their corrective bases.

5) Trade Management & Risk Controls

The market backdrop now supports more offense, but the lack of strong momentum means risk still needs to be managed deliberately. This is a “press selectively” environment, not a “buy everything” environment.

Risk controls

  • Use ¾ normal size for clean setups in leading groups.

  • Use full size only for the best leaders with tight risk, strong relative strength, and proper entries.

  • Use ½ size for secondary-sector names that are still emerging from bases.

  • Take partial profits into fast strength if a stock becomes extended quickly.

  • Trail faster leaders with the 10-day moving average.

  • Use the 20-day moving average for slower swing positions that are acting well.

  • If a stock breaks out and quickly fails back into the base, cut it quickly.

  • If breadth stays strong, give leaders a little more room. If breadth weakens, tighten stops aggressively.

6) Exposure Controls & Scenarios

Base Case: Constructive Advance, Breadth Improving

The major indices are acting well, large caps are making new near-term highs, mid/small caps are pushing higher after reclaiming support, and breadth is positive.

Exposure: 65–80% of normal
Cash: 15–30%
Posture: Constructive, selective, offensively engaged

The goal is to participate in leadership while keeping enough flexibility to manage volatility or buy clean pullbacks.

Bullish Expansion Scenario

This develops if Technology continues to lead, secondary groups break out of bases, new highs continue to expand, new lows stay contained, and momentum begins to accelerate.

Action: Increase exposure toward 80–90%.

  • Press the best leaders.

  • Add to clean breakouts and tight continuation patterns.

  • Expand beyond Technology only into sectors showing true relative strength improvement.

Constructive Grind Scenario

This develops if indices continue higher, breadth remains positive, but momentum remains modest.

Action: Maintain 65–75% exposure.

  • Focus on high-quality setups only.

  • Take profits into extension.

  • Avoid overtrading.

  • This is still a good environment, but not one that rewards sloppy entries.

Rotation / Mixed Leadership Scenario

This develops if Technology remains strong but secondary groups fail to confirm, while Energy and defensives continue breaking down.

Action: Keep exposure near 60–70%.

  • Stay concentrated in true leadership.

  • Avoid weak sectors.

  • Do not assume broad participation until the charts confirm it.

Failed Breakout / Breadth Reversal Scenario

This develops if large caps reverse from new highs, lose the 10-day moving average, mid/small caps weaken, and new lows begin expanding again.

Action: Reduce exposure toward 45–60%.

  • Cut failed breakouts quickly.

  • Stop adding to extended names.

  • Raise cash and wait for the next reset.

Bottom Line

The market backdrop has improved. Large caps are making new near-term highs, mid- and small-caps are pushing higher after a successful 50-day moving average bounce, and breadth has broadened with new highs more than doubling new lows. That supports a more constructive tactical posture.

The main caution is that momentum still has not fully accelerated. Participation is improving, but many stocks are grinding higher rather than expanding powerfully. The right approach is to press selectively: stay focused on Technology leadership, begin watching emerging secondary groups, avoid Energy and defensive breakdowns, and increase exposure only through clean setups with defined risk.
